title: Concatenate values that may be null

blocks.text: `+` never fails on `null`: it inserts the four letters `"null"`, so `"Hello" + null` is `"Hellonull"`. `"Hello".concat(null)` throws `NullPointerException` instead. Neither is what a reader wants to see, so a value that may be `null` is checked before it is joined.
Write `address(String title, String name)` in `Greeting`. It returns the title and the name separated by one space, leaving out whichever is `null`:

cases.says: address("Dr", null) is "Dr", and address(null, null) is "".

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: + turns null into the text "null", while concat(null) throws, so a value that may be null is checked first.
